note: Curation input, hand-written. build-practice-corpus.py turns it into corpus.json + assets.

items.alt: A team of donkeys drawing a flat wooden cart on motor-car wheels along a dirt road, with two men riding on it.
items.tell: The rig is improvised — a timber bed on a steel frame, motor-car wheels, chain traces — and every joint still closes: chain from the animals to the shaft, shaft to the cart, wheel on the hub it turns on. Trace the linkage before you call it. Working vehicles are often ugly and always connected.

items.commons_title: File:Frying red pine mushrooms in a pan (54064465568).jpg
items.alt: Orange mushrooms and sliced onion cooking in a pan with a wooden spoon.
items.tell: Every piece is a consistent part of one mushroom species — cap, gilled underside and stalk in the right relationship — and each cut edge matches the flesh it came from. Real food varies in size; it never varies in anatomy.

items.commons_title: File:Capsicum baccatum in Saúde flea market, São Paulo, Brazil.jpg
items.alt: Rows of small coloured plastic bowls holding chillies, berries and beans on a market stall.
items.tell: Rows of near-identical bowls look like a tiled texture, and tiling is a genuine tell — but here each bowl holds a different count heaped to a different height with its own shadow. Repetition with variation is a stall; repetition without it is a texture.

items.alt: A person driving a small tractor along a grass track, with four baskets of leafy seedlings carried on a rear frame.
items.tell: An unfamiliar machine is not an impossible one. Follow it through: the operator sits over the drive, the crates rest on the bed that carries them, and the flattened track behind matches its wheels.

items.commons_title: File:Mixed mushroom buns, pan fried - San Francisco, CA.jpg
items.alt: Three round sesame-topped buns arranged on a long dark plate, seen from directly above.
items.tell: An overhead food shot is the format generators imitate, so the reflex is to distrust it. The seeds settle it: the scatter is different on every bun, seeds sit on the crust and on the cloth around the plate, and no two buns share an outline.

items.commons_title: File:Hotel De Oriente Philippines late 1800's to early 1900's.jpg
items.alt: A colonnaded street of a grand arcaded building at low sun, with a horse and a covered carriage standing on the cobbles.
items.tell: Nothing connects the horse to the carriage. There are no shafts, no traces and no swingletree — the harness straps end in mid-air on the animal's flank while the vehicle stands behind it as though being drawn. Look for the load path before you look at the style.

items.alt: A donkey drawing a wooden cart along a dirt road, a man standing on the cart behind a person lying under a blanket.
items.tell: The painted finish is not the evidence — paintings are not fakes, and a photograph can be styled to look like one. The wheel is: a third spoked wheel stands under the donkey's belly, ahead of the cart's own wheel and on a different line, joined to no axle, no frame and no hub. Ask what carries the load before you judge the surface.

items.alt: A dark bowl of golden fried mushroom pieces scattered with chopped herbs, on a dark wooden table.
items.tell: Several pieces are cuts no mushroom has — a dark gilled hollow opening in the middle of a smooth dome, and a piece that closes into a hollow ring. Food is a good place to look: texture is easy to fake, anatomy is not.

items.alt: A flat-panel monitor showing a goldfish, standing in long meadow grass under a bright sun and scattered cloud.
items.tell: The monitor is mounted on a slab that is half keyboard and half plinth — not a laptop, not a stand, not any object that could hold a screen up. Generators assemble the PARTS of familiar things without the joint that makes them work.

items.alt: A still life of mushrooms, preserving jars, a bowl of red-capped fungi and books on a cloth-covered table.
items.tell: Look at the tall jar. Its contents repeat as near-identical stamped discs in rows, which is a tiled texture rather than a jar of real produce, and the loose mushrooms do not settle on one species — one cap is furred, its neighbour smooth, and the same stalk carries both gills and pores.

items.commons_title: File:Aux cuisines du chateau, une corne dabondance IA Dall e Bing 18 nov 2023 Lamiot 01.png
items.alt: A wicker cornucopia spilling fruit and gourds across a bare wooden table against dark panelling.
items.tell: The horn is woven in believable rows at its mouth, then the weave dissolves into a smooth spiral at the tip that no basket could be made in. Regular manufactured pattern that stops being regular is the tell.

items.commons_title: File:Kaplica grobowa rodziny Potockich P1680784 Peczera.jpg
items.alt: A small stone church with a rounded apse standing among yellow autumn trees under a deep blue sky.
items.tell: The colour is doing the lying here, not the picture. Saturation is a processing choice; what matters is that the stone courses run continuously into the curve of the apse and the shadows all agree. Vivid is not evidence.

items.alt: A tiny chapel on a rocky summit at night, one window lit, under a dark streaked sky.
items.tell: It looks impossible because it is a long exposure. A slow shutter is what smears cloud into streaks and turns one small lamp into a steady glow. An unusual camera setting is not an artefact.

items.commons_title: File:Keble College Chapel Exterior, Oxford, UK - Diliff.jpg
items.alt: A large Victorian chapel in banded red and cream brick with tall traceried windows, on a lawn under a blue sky.
items.tell: The brick banding is so regular that it reads as a tiled texture. Check it the way you would check a generator: the bands run unbroken around every corner and behind every downpipe, and every buttress shadow falls the same way. Regularity that survives inspection is masonry.

items.alt: A long baroque brick palace with pale stone dressings, seen across a wide expanse of wind-rippled water.
items.tell: Wind has broken the moat into chop, so there is no mirror image to check — and that is not suspicious. A rippled surface scatters the sky instead of returning the building; you only get a reflection when the water is still. What holds instead is the waterline: the chop shrinks and its contrast falls smoothly towards the far bank, the swans sit in the water rather than on it, and the balustrade shadows agree with the sun. An absent reflection is a fact about the weather, not about the pipeline.

items.commons_title: File:AI generated Image Marienkapelle Zeil am Main 1727.jpg
items.alt: A small stone chapel with a tiled roof and a roof cross, on a grassy hilltop behind dry-stone walls.
items.tell: The picture wears late golden light, yet nothing in it has a shadow — not the chapel, not the bush, not the dry-stone wall. Both faces of the building are lit equally, so there is no direction to the sun at all. A generator copies the LOOK of late light without running the geometry that light implies.

items.alt: A lakeside promenade with benches, lamp-posts and many visitors, a city skyline and a large statue across the water.
items.tell: The sun is hard enough to put crisp shadows under the visitors and their benches, yet the lamp-posts and the parapet lay none at all on the paving. It is the DISAGREEMENT that convicts, not the absence: objects sharing one plaza share one sun, and this scene was lit item by item instead of being solved once.

items.alt: An elevated view over a city of glass towers threaded with waterways, woodland and low roofs with solar panels.
items.tell: Glass is a mirror. These towers are glazed top to bottom in bright hazy sun and not one pane returns anything — no sky, no cloud, no neighbouring tower, no bright edge where a face turns — while the ponds below them mirror the trees perfectly well. Ask what a surface ought to be reflecting, not only where the shadows are.

items.alt: A busy open-air market street lined with stalls under canopies, with many shoppers walking between them.
items.tell: This is what a real crowd encodes: different trades, ages and styles of dress in one frame, some people carrying loads on the head and some not. A generated crowd tends to dress everybody the same way.

items.commons_title: File:People purchasing Mangoes in Powerpowet station road.jpg
items.alt: A narrow city street with parked motorcycles, a handcart and shopfronts with painted signs.
items.tell: The signage is the check, and you do not need to read the script to run it: the same letterforms recur, correctly formed, across two lines of one board and again on its neighbours, with a global brand name spelled correctly among the local ones. Generated signage melts between signs into letter-shaped marks.

items.commons_title: File:2024 Kapliczka Matki Bożej w Jaszkowej Górnej (1).jpg
items.alt: A small whitewashed wayside shrine with a domed top and an arched opening, standing beside an overgrown bank.
items.tell: An unfamiliar building type reads as invented, and this is a real vernacular form. The render, the water staining and the vegetation are all consistent with one neglected structure. Unfamiliar is not the same as wrong.

items.alt: A large hall of students in white polo shirts and face masks writing at individual desks.
items.tell: The crest and lettering on the uniform dissolve into unreadable marks at a resolution where individual stitches are sharp. An institution's insignia is a claim about which institution — and this one names nothing.

items.commons_title: File:Sanctuary of Ercole Vincitore Tivoli Render Model Inside Gemini-generated.png
items.alt: A wide sunlit plaza before a columned temple, crowded with people in robes, with tiered stone seating to one side.
items.tell: Look for what people are DOING, not what they wear. The stalls stand laden but nobody buys, nobody carries a load, leads an animal or works; and the tiered seating is full of an audience facing an empty plaza with nothing staged in front of it. The generator drew a population and forgot to give it business.
